summary: The change renames the routine schedule protocol to automation schedules end to end. The new snapshot route accepts only POST, so a GET for an automation with the id "schedules" still reaches the state route, and the edited durable test checks this. I accept the replies to F1 and F2: published 0.1.68 already serves automations.runScheduled. The change is still not ready. The temp test run fails because AutomationScheduleSync.test.ts imports a fixture that does not exist, so AutomationScheduleSync and ControlPlaneScheduleReporter show as uncovered. Five reformatted PostgreSQL-path lines are also uncovered and not exempt.

findings.body: The test imports `automationTest` from `../fixtures.test.js`, but `src/automations/fixtures.test.ts` does not exist. The only fixtures are `src/routines/fixtures.test.ts`, which exports `routineTest`, and `src/storage/fixtures.test.ts`. The suite fails to load with "Cannot find module '../fixtures.test.js'", so none of its tests run. That leaves the new activation-type filter in AutomationScheduleSync (lines 31, 37, 61, 65, 74) untested. The failed suite also makes the temp run exit 1, and no coverage was recorded for ControlPlaneScheduleReporter. Fix: import an existing fixture, such as `routineTest` from `../../routines/fixtures.test.js` with `routines.automations` as the AutomationService, or construct the fixture inside the temp test. Then confirm both temp test files pass.

testRequests.target: packages/workspace-server/src/automations/AutomationScheduleSync.ts:31,37,61,65,74: the published snapshot contains only enabled automations of type "routine" that have a nextRunAt, excluding trigger automations and disabled routines, and it is published again after changes.
testRequests.rationale: The temp test already written for this does not load (F3). After the import is fixed, it must pass and cover these lines.
The existing reporter temp test passed, but these lines show as uncovered because the temp run failed as a whole. They must be covered after F3 is fixed.

These lines are uncovered and not exempt. Either cover them by running the opt-in PostgreSQL test (HALO_TEST_POSTGRES_URL), or add coverage-exempt comments. I would accept a reason such as "PostgreSQL-only branch; the unit suite runs SQLite; the change is only a type-checked field rename and reformat".
